questions.question: What is the safest first step when Python raises a traceback?
options: Read the exception type/message and the failing line in your code.
Delete the function and start again.
Catch all exceptions with bare `except`.
Ignore it if the code works sometimes.
questions.explanation: Traceback type and location are the fastest route to diagnosis.

questions.question: Why is bare `except:` considered risky?
options: It is always a syntax error.
It can hide unexpected bugs and swallow important exceptions.
It only catches ValueError.
It makes code run slower than loops.
questions.explanation: Specific exceptions keep debugging signals visible.

questions.question: Which inputs should tests include beyond happy-path values?
options: Only random large numbers.
Only the exact example shown in docs.
Empty, invalid, boundary, zero/negative, and duplicate cases.
No edge cases if code looks correct.
questions.explanation: Edge cases expose assumptions that normal inputs hide.

questions.question: What does `assert x > 0` do?
options: Skips the check in all modes.
Prints whether x is positive.
Converts x into a positive number.
Raises AssertionError if the condition is false.
questions.explanation: Assertions encode expected conditions and fail loudly when violated.

questions.question: When should you raise a new exception?
options: When input/state violates a function contract and caller must know.
Whenever you want to stop code quickly, regardless of context.
Never; always return None.
Only inside class methods.
questions.explanation: Raise with clear messages when contracts are violated and recovery is not local.

questions.question: Which tool ensures cleanup runs whether or not an exception occurs?
options: continue statement
finally block (or equivalent context manager cleanup).
break statement
assert statement
questions.explanation: finally guarantees cleanup execution on both success and failure paths.

questions.question: What is a reliable debugging workflow?
options: Suppress the exception and continue.
Change many lines quickly and rerun once.
Reproduce, inspect, hypothesize, change one thing, retest.
Ask the AI for a full rewrite immediately.
questions.explanation: Controlled, iterative debugging reduces noise and isolates root causes.

questions.question: What is the best reason to keep tests around after fixing a bug?
options: They force every function to use classes.
They eliminate all need for logging.
They make exceptions unnecessary.
They prevent the same bug from silently returning.
questions.explanation: Regression tests lock in corrected behavior.
